marble.name: Apostrophes for possession
marble.subject: English
marble.description: Use the possessive apostrophe with singular nouns to show ownership (e.g., the girl's book, the dog's bone)
marble.prompt: When you writes something belonging to one person or thing — like "the dog's lead" or "the girl's bag" — do they put the apostrophe in the right place?

cluster.summary: Your child is learning to spell by connecting sounds to letters — building simple words, adding common endings like -ing and -ed, and memorising important words that don't follow regular spelling patterns.

authoredAnswer: "The horse's mane was long." (one horse owns the mane: horse + 's). "The horses galloped away." (plural, nothing belongs, so no apostrophe). "Ravi's lunchbox."

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: Adds an apostrophe to plain plurals because the word ends in s. Evidence basis: DfE (2013), National curriculum in England: English Appendix 1, spelling, Year 2. This is an authored observable performance check against t
wrongAnswers.fix: Ask "What belongs to the horses?"; if nothing, there is no apostrophe. Match three more sentences to pictures.

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: Omits the apostrophe or places it on the owned item. Evidence basis: DfE (2013), National curriculum in England: English Appendix 1, spelling, Year 2. This is an authored observable performance check against the source-b
wrongAnswers.fix: Use the "belonging to" card: find the owner, write it in full, then add 's straight after it.
